intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that arthrogryposis multiplex congenita-9 with immunodeficiency (AMC9) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SENP7 gene.

checks.claim: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita-9 with immunodeficiency (AMC9) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SENP7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified a homozygous stop gain variant in SENP7 c.1474C>T; p.(Gln492*) as the probable aetiology.
checks.explanation: The paper names a homozygous SENP7 variant as the probable cause of the arthrogryposis syndrome. The AMC9 label is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita-9 with immunodeficiency (AMC9) is an autosomal recessive disorder that is lethal in infancy or before birth. Features include congenital arthrogryposis, failure to achieve developmental milestones, early respiratory failure, neutropenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and recurrent infections (Samra et al., 2023; Kobayashi et al., 2024). Prenatally detected anomalies have included central nervous system malformations, congenital heart disease, and renal anomalies (Saad et al., 2025).

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a kindred with AMC9, Samra et al. (2023) used exome sequencing and segregation studies to identify a homozygous nonsense mutation in the SENP7 gene (c.1474C-T; gln492-to-ter, Q492X). Fibroblasts from the proband showed decreased SENP7 mRNA expression. Protein expression studies showed significant protein dysregulation in total cell lysates and in the chromatin fraction. Patient fibroblasts also had reduced levels of HP1-alpha, several histones, and H3K9me3. The authors suggested that loss of SENP7 leads to reduced heterochromatin condensation and aberrant gene expression.

paragraphs.text: In 4 affected infants from a kindred with AMC9, Samra et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.1474C-T transition in the SENP7 gene that resulted in a gln492-to-ter (Q492X) substitution. The mutation was found by exome sequencing, and segregation studies were performed. Proband fibroblasts showed decreased SENP7 mRNA expression and reduced levels of HP1-alpha, histones, and H3K9me3. All affected infants died within 4 months after birth.
